name: Mairang
description: District headquarters of Eastern West Khasi Hills, a historic hill town about 40 km from Shillong on the route to Nongstoin. Known as the home of freedom fighter U Tirot Sing Syiem and as a base for exploring Kyllang Rock, valleys, and Khasi cultural sites.
facts: Headquarters of Eastern West Khasi Hills district (created 2021)
About 40 km from Shillong along NH-106
Associated with U Tirot Sing and Anglo-Khasi War

name: Kyllang Rock
description: Massive granite monolith dome rising about 1,774 m (5,820 ft), located roughly 9-12 km northwest of Mairang. Steeped in Khasi folklore as a personified figure who battled Symper Rock; offers panoramic views after a short climb, with rare white rhododendrons nearby.
facts: Large granitic dome about 1,000 feet wide
Accessible from northern and eastern flanks
Linked to Khasi legends of battle with Symper Rock

name: Mawthadraishan Peak
description: Highest point in Eastern West Khasi Hills at 1,924.5 metres (6,314 ft), midway between Mairang and Nongstoin. Offers 360-degree panoramic views of the Khasi Hills, Garo Hills, and distant Himalayas on clear days, with natural ponds on the range.
facts: Highest elevation in the district at 1,924.5 m
Views of Assam plains and Himalayas post-monsoon

name: Ka Phan Nonglait Falls
description: Serene waterfall near Mairang, named after the unsung Khasi woman warrior Phan Nonglait who aided U Tirot Sing against the British by disarming soldiers at the falls during the Anglo-Khasi War. Surrounded by lush forests.
facts: Named after female freedom fighter Phan Nonglait
Site linked to events of the Anglo-Khasi War

name: Tirot Sing Ecological Park
description: Park in Mairangbah village featuring a statue of U Tirot Sing, an old colonial-era pine tree, children's play area, and views of sunrise and sunset over Mairang town. Combines history, recreation, and local culture.
facts: Features statue of freedom fighter U Tirot Sing
Good sunrise and sunset views of the town

name: Markham and Remkhla Valley
description: Rolling green hills and valleys near Markham and Mawkyllei villages, locally known as Laitmurok viewpoint. Famous for misty mornings, grassland meadows, and scenic rural landscapes; often compared to a mini Dzukou Valley.
facts: Situated near Markham and Mawkyllei villages
Known for unique beauty and grazing lands
Border area with South West Khasi Hills
Emerging offbeat destination for nature lovers

name: Laitarted Lake
description: Popular tourist attraction lake in Eastern West Khasi Hills, offering a peaceful natural setting amid the hills for visitors seeking quiet outdoor experiences.
facts: Listed among popular attractions of the district

name: Kynshi River (Eastern West Khasi Hills section)
description: Major river coursing through Eastern West Khasi Hills with tributaries featuring rapids, waterfalls, and stunning riverine terrain. Enhanced by silver reeds in season; popular for scenic views and potential adventure.
facts: Flows as an artery through the district
Part of the broader Kynshi river system

name: Mawkyrwat
description: Headquarters of South West Khasi Hills district, a hill town about 75 km from Shillong. Serves as a gateway to the district's caves, hot springs, viewpoints, and border areas near Bangladesh.
facts: District HQ of South West Khasi Hills (formed 2012)
Base for exploring Jakrem, Ranikor, and local viewpoints

name: Jakrem Hot Spring
description: Natural sulphur hot spring near Jakrem village, about 15 km from Mawkyrwat and 60 km from Shillong. Popular picnic spot in winter; water is believed to have medicinal properties for skin ailments.
facts: Located at Lawblei (Jakrem) on Shillong-Mawkyrwat road

name: Symper Rock
description: Unique geological monolith formation about 50 km from Shillong on the Shillong-Mawkyrwat road. Linked to Khasi folklore of a battle with Kyllang Rock; offers views of the Mawkyrwat area from the top.
facts: Also known as Lum Symper or Sympher Rock
Part of Khasi legend involving fight with Kyllang

name: Umngi River
description: Longest river in the Mawkyrwat subdivision, originating near Sohiong and flowing to Umpung Lake. Features a small river island used for beach volleyball and serves as a popular local picnic and angling spot about 18 km from Mawkyrwat.
facts: Small river island in its course

name: Phlangja Ud Cave
description: Beautiful cave about 16 km from Mawkyrwat south of Rangmaw village. Features hanging stalactites; above it lies vast grassland offering views of Bangladesh plains. Cave length about 600 meters.
facts: Located at Phlangja Ud near Rangmaw
Grassland above cave with Bangladesh views

name: Rilang View Point
description: Scenic viewpoint and valley about 5 km from Mawkyrwat at Mawranglang on the Nongstoin-Mawkyrwat road. Meandering across the river, it is a convenient picnic and angling spot.

name: Synrangbah Cave
description: Yawning open cave at Nonglang about 3 km from Mawkyrwat. The Mawkyrwat-Photjaud road passes through its leveled interior; used as shelter during rain and home to bats of various sizes.
facts: Shelter for people and cattle in storms

name: Dongnob Falls
description: Beautiful waterfall about 8 km from Mawkyrwat at Photjaud. Features a cave in the middle that becomes a splendid natural beauty in winter with sun ray reflections.

name: Iawpaw Plateau
description: Beautiful tableland about 30 km from Mawkyrwat southwest of Nongnah. Offers bird’s-eye views of surrounding hills, valleys, Bangladesh plains and rivers, and the Himalayas. Contains one of the longest caves in Khasi Hills; looks like a bed from a distance.
facts: Views of Bangladesh plains and Himalayas
Longest cave in Khasi Hills on the plateau

name: Ranikor
description: Border town about 45 km from Mawkyrwat, close to Bangladesh, formerly a winter resort of the queen of Maharam. Famous for angling Golden Mahseers, boat rowing, and the Borba Singh Bridge (second longest suspension bridge in India). Hosts an annual tourism festival.
facts: Borba Singh Bridge over the river
Best spot for Golden Mahseer angling
